invalid_claims: Renaming work completion (e.g., inlets cleared, windows latched, items secured, cordons placed) as measured storm benefit or avoided harm.

Unvalidated mechanical failure thresholds (`glass_capacity_pa`: [1200, 2400], `structure_capacity_pa`: [500, 1800], `tree_dry_anchorage_gust_mps`: [35, 55]) and arbitrary `sensitivity_multipliers` ([0.65, 1, 1.35]) that have no empirical basis in the provided catalog.

Unverified site-specific elevation and electrical parameters (`entry_threshold_m`: 0.15, `barrier_rating_m`: 0.6, `service_panel_threshold_m`: 0.45, `backup_flood_threshold_m`: 0.8, `generator_kw`: 20, `load_kw`: 10) applied to mapped assets without local condition surveys.

Assigning building power outage causality via geometric nearest-feeder association from `pge` or `cec` maps, which explicitly do not establish customer service connections, overhead vs. underground status, or live outage probability.

Treating observational literature associations (`uf-trees`: 73% vs. 47% tree survival after Hurricane Andrew) or forensic mitigable-cause judgments (`sf-glass`: 30 of 31 broken panes judged mitigable) as causal treatment effects or failure probability reductions.
Treating historical 311 requests (`sf-311`) or public works service order counts (`sf-works`) as verified ground-truth component failures, current defects, or local risk calibration.

Claiming whole-building structural protection from opening protection (`fema-michael`) or applying light wood-frame bracing mechanisms (`fema-andrew`) to mapped San Francisco buildings of unknown structural system (`engineered-support`).
smallest_defensible_model: A paired, deterministic (or matched-seed) conditional scenario comparator running on the 3D asset geometry (`buildings`, `tree-map`, `street-map`) under identical user-specified spatial storm forcing (wind pressure/gust fields and flood water depth $d_w(x,y)$). Instead of uncalibrated fragility curves or failure probabilities, each asset and operation is evaluated using explicit, user-stated conditional state variables and threshold inequalities. Under identical forcing, the model computes binary component state differences (with vs. without preventive action) strictly for mechanisms supported by documented physical regimes: (1) doorway water entry blocked if $h_{\text{entry}} < d_w \le h_{\text{barrier}}$ for a complete barrier (`fit-barrier`, `sandbag-wall`), and overtopped if $d_w > h_{\text{barrier}}$ (`sandy`); (2) relocated contents (`move-contents`) transitioning from inundated to dry when $h_{\text{orig}} < d_w \le h_{\text{new}}$; (3) emergency pumping (`backup-pump`) maintaining water control during an assumed grid outage if and only if flood depth remains below the lowest supporting component elevation ($d_w \le \min(h_{\text{gen}}, h_{\text{switch}}, h_{\text{fuel}})$) and $P_{\text{gen}} \ge P_{\text{pump}}$ (`sandy`); and (4) explicit hazard-source state removal for addressed pre-existing conditions (loose debris sources removed via `secure-items`, open windows closed via `latch-windows`, surface inlet litter removed via `clear-inlet`, route debris removed via `clear-route`, or exposure access restricted via `install-cordon`) reported purely as conditional physical state changes without uncalibrated failure probabilities or dollar damage.
real_storm_validation_needed: Test the flood barrier overtopping regime against `sandy` (FEMA P-942): verify that the numerical model transitions from 'entry blocked' to 'overtopped/flooded' exactly when local water elevation exceeds the barrier's verified design rating ($d_w > h_{\text{barrier}}$) or when a sandbag wall (`fema234`) is incomplete.

Test the backup power and pump dependency chain against `sandy` (FEMA P-942): verify that simulated backup systems maintain water control when pumps are connected to emergency power and all supporting components remain dry, but fail completely when transfer switches, fuel equipment, or pumps are submerged ($d_w > h_{\text{component}}$) even if the generator itself is elevated.

Test the building envelope vs. structural vulnerability separation against `fema-michael`: verify that securing openings (`latch-windows`) does not suppress independent structural or roof failure modes in the model.

Test glazing failure mode separation against `sf-glass`: verify that removing loose exterior items (`secure-items`) or latching operable windows (`latch-windows`) only alters the corresponding conditional mechanism flags (windborne debris source count or open-window state) and does not alter intact glass pressure capacity or existing glass defects.
Label all benchmark tests strictly as mechanism validation (verifying that model equations reproduce documented physical failure regimes), never as local San Francisco risk calibration.
supported_now: 3D spatial rendering of mapped asset footprints and centerlines (`buildings`, `tree-map`, `street-map`, `pge`, `cec`) paired with historical 311 report locations (`sf-311`) labeled strictly as 'locations to re-check/inspect'.
Resource, crew-role, equipment bill-of-materials, and bounded task-time accounting (work minutes + setup overhead + travel allowance) for the 11 documented operations.

Conditional binary state comparison (With vs. Without intervention under identical storm forcing) for doorway flood barriers (`fit-barrier`, `sandbag-wall`) given user-input threshold elevation $h_{\text{entry}}$, design rating $h_{\text{barrier}}$, and local water depth $d_w$.
Conditional binary exposure comparison for relocated portable contents (`move-contents`) given user-input initial elevation, target storage elevation, and local flood depth $d_w$.

Conditional logic-tree evaluation for backup pump operation (`backup-pump`) during an assumed outage, conditioned on user-input elevations for switches, fuel, and generator relative to local flood depth $d_w$.

Conditional physical precondition state tracking (under identical forcing) for removing specified counts of accessible loose debris sources (`secure-items`), closing confirmed open/unlatched windows (`latch-windows`), clearing confirmed surface-only inlet litter (`clear-inlet`), clearing light road debris (`clear-route`), and placing authorized closures (`install-cordon`), where benefit is strictly zero if the precondition (e.g., debris present, window unlatched) is absent.
cannot_identify_now: Dollar damages, financial losses, or monetized return on investment (no cost or damage-function evidence exists in the catalog).

Absolute or relative failure probabilities for glass breakage, structural framing failure, or street tree windthrow in San Francisco (`glass_capacity_pa`, `structure_capacity_pa`, and `tree_dry_anchorage_gust_mps` are unvalidated).
Causal reduction in tree failure probability from `prune-defect` (`uf-trees` provides an external observational survival association from Hurricane Andrew, not a causal or local treatment effect).

Causal flood-depth reduction or avoided building damage per cleared catch basin from `clear-inlet` (`sf-works` and `drain-time` provide operational guidance and time budgets, not hydraulic drainage capacity or subsurface pipe data).
Building-specific grid outage probabilities or cascading electrical failures from `pge` and `cec` maps (feeder-to-building connectivity and overhead/underground vulnerability are unestablished).

Structural collapse prevention or load-capacity increases from `engineered-support` on mapped SF buildings (building structural systems and defects are unknown; `fema-andrew` applies to light wood-frame failures).
Avoided injury counts or traffic safety rates from `install-cordon` or `clear-route`.
implementation_plan: Step 1: Strip all unvalidated fragility parameters (`glass_capacity_pa`, `structure_capacity_pa`, `tree_dry_anchorage_gust_mps`, `sensitivity_multipliers`), nearest-feeder outage rules, and any UI labels that equate task completion with avoided harm.

Step 2: Implement a paired counterfactual state engine that ingests a single 3D spatial storm forcing field (flood depth $d_w(x,y)$ and wind indicator $w(x,y)$) and evaluates every asset twice—once with the selected operations applied and once without—holding forcing and all conditional site inputs identical.

Step 3: Replace hardcoded building/electrical parameters with an explicit 'Conditional Site Assumptions' input layer (defaulting to 'Unverified / User Input Required' unless specified for a scenario) for $h_{\text{entry}}$, $h_{\text{barrier}}$, $h_{\text{switch}}$, $h_{\text{gen}}$, and pre-existing defect flags (e.g., `has_surface_debris`, `unlatched_window_count`, `loose_item_count`).

Step 4: Encode the supported physical mechanism equations: barrier overtopping inequality ($h_{\text{entry}} < d_w \le h_{\text{barrier}}$), content elevation inequality ($h_{\text{orig}} < d_w \le h_{\text{new}}$), series-system backup power survival ($d_w \le \min(h_{\text{chain}})$), and precondition state toggles (setting benefit to zero if the baseline defect is not present or if multi-step operations like `sandbag-wall` are incomplete before storm arrival).

Step 5: Build an automated validation test suite that runs the engine against the documented real-storm cases (`sandy` floodgate overtopping, `sandy` submerged transfer switch vs. functional backup pump, `fema-michael` shuttered building with non-window vulnerability) and displays a 'Mechanism Validation vs. Uncalibrated Local Risk' audit badge in the 3D UI.

Step 6: Update the 3D spatial visualization to render side-by-side or diffed physical states (e.g., 'Water Entry Blocked vs. Flooded (Overtopped)', 'Backup Pump Active vs. Defeated by Submerged Switch', 'Precondition Hazard Removed vs. Exposed') while explicitly locking out unsupported numerical comparisons (tree pruning survival delta, structural capacity delta, feeder outage probability, and dollar damages).
